paragraphs.source_en: Equally symbolic, perhaps, was the joint campaign of the Latins and Romans against Nur al-​Din. The atabeg released a few thousand prisoners and offered to assist Manuel with his wars in Asia Minor, which sufficed. Manuel was now, and for the rest of his reign, the chief protector of Outremer. He impressed the Antiochenes with his skill at jousting. Part of the objective, as the court orator Eustathios put it years later, was to gather up “living pearls and stones, from the whole earth . . . [to] encircle your crown.”82 Manuel’s goal was not to dominate the Latins, but to open his east Roman world to them and make them feel that it was also part of their own. This was an aspect of his notorious Latinophilia, which was criticized and resented by some of his subjects.
